 LIFESTYLE Personal Finance Are you getting your Social Security Payment this Wednesday? Completes of beneficiaries that will get their deposit
 Veterans Day has changed the usual November payment calendar, meaning some recipients will receive their money earlier than expected
 Social Security Administration 
 BRANDON SUTTON (SAM)
 Editor Editor Updated 16/11/2026

 Personal Finance.  Average Social Security check at age 65: How much will you get for 2027 with the COLA for next year? 
 Personal Finance.  Can you just walk into a Social Security office without an appointment? These are the few cases when you can do it 
 Millions of Americans receiving Social Security benefits will notice a change to the usual November payment schedule, with the Veterans Day federal holiday affecting when some deposits arrive as the adjustment means certain beneficiaries will receive their money earlier.
Although payments later in the month will follow the regular calendar, Social Security normally distributes retirement benefits according to recipients' dates of birth. Those born between the first and 10th typically receive their money on the second Wednesday, which was November 11.
 Ronaldinho returns to soccer against Forli at 46 and shows he’s still the king of Joga Bonito Whilst beneficiaries born between the 11th and 20th are paid on the third Wednesday, on November 18 and finally, those born between the 21st and 31st receive their deposits on the fourth Wednesday on November 25th.
But November's calendar introduces an exception because Veterans Day fell on Wednesday, November 11 since federal benefit payments are not normally issued on federal holidays, the affected payment has been moved forward by one day.
That means eligible recipients will receive their money on Tuesday, November 10 whilst the remaining November payments are scheduled to follow the usual Wednesday arrangement.
Beneficiaries should therefore check their birth-date category before assuming their deposit has been delayed or that the entire monthly schedule has changed.
 Social Security is an important benefit to seniors in the United States Bernie Sanders pushes for an additional $2,400 in Social Security benefits
 While recipients prepare for their November deposits, Senator Bernie Sanders is continuing his campaign to increase Social Security payments through his proposed Social Security Expansion Act - introduced in February 2025 alongside Senator Elizabeth Warren and other lawmakers.
The act would provide eligible beneficiaries with an additional $2,400 annually, equivalent to $200 per month as the legislation would cover retired workers, people receiving disability benefits and surviving family members. It also proposes changing how annual cost-of-living adjustments are calculated.
Instead of using the standard formula of Customer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers (CPI-W) , Sanders , representing Vermont . proposes using the Consumer Price Index for the Elderly (CPI-E) to better reflect the spending patterns of older Americans .
Other provisions include restoring certain student benefits for eligible children of deceased or disabled workers up to age 22, alongside improvements to the special minimum benefit for people with lengthy careers and relatively low earnings – and funding the proposed expansion is another central part of Sanders ' plan.
He wants to remove the existing cap on earnings subject to Social Security payroll taxes, requiring higher-income Americans to contribute taxes on a greater portion of their earnings as Sanders has argued that the changes could strengthen the program's finances over the next 75 years.
He also argues that providing meaningful additional support to beneficiaries. He has also identified benefit expansion and long-term financial security as priorities for the next Congress and the proposal could receive renewed attention as soon as January 2027.
That’s when Sanders is expected to take over as chair of the Senate Finance Subcommittee on Social Security and whilst the legislation would still need congressional approval before any proposed increases could become reality, the Democrats now control the House and could approve the policy.
